findings.claim: The kmctl-read plugin passes paths straight to Hermes' read and search handlers, which read anywhere the runner user can, not only the repository. Their guards are a denylist, and Hermes' own docstring says 'This is NOT a security boundary'. Run against Hermes 0.19.0 with a fresh HOME, the handlers read /etc/hostname and /home/vscode/.bashrc. They refuse /proc/*/environ for read_file, but search_files with output_mode count on /proc/PID/environ returns 1 for 'KMKEY=bfkey-s' and 0 for 'KMKEY=bfkey-x'. That is a prefix test a model can repeat to recover the provider key one character at a time. A non-sk- key (Ollama, Bifrost virtual keys, a custom gateway) has no known prefix, so redaction does not mask it. The findings text goes into a public issue, so a prompt planted in audited content could leak the key there. The config file is safe: it holds the literal ${KMKEY}, not the key. The plan should have the plugin resolve every path (following symlinks) and refuse any path outside the repository root, which also covers /proc and HOME. Its tests (r3 or r2) should show reads and searches outside the repo, including a count search on /proc/self/environ, are refused.

Round 1: the plugin's tools read outside the repository and a count search on /proc/PID/environ leaks the key. The plan now resolves every path, follows symlinks, refuses anything outside the audited root, and r3 tests /proc/self/environ in count mode and a symlink out of the repo.

The path guard does not cover the search pattern. Hermes' search builds `rg --line-number --no-heading --with-filename '<pattern>' '<path>'` with no `-e` or `--`, so a pattern that starts with a dash is read as an rg flag. Through the real 0.19.0 handler, pattern `--pre=rm` with the repo as path deleted every file in the working folder, and `--pre=/bin/sh` ran a shell script from the repo (it wrote a file outside it). That is command execution in the step that holds the API key: it breaks read-only (I2), and it gets around the path guard, since a script can read /proc/self/environ. The grep fallback has the same flaw. The plugin must refuse patterns that start with '-' (or run its own search with `-e`/`--`), and should pass the resolved absolute path on to the handler so a path cannot start with '-' either. r3 should check that a dash-leading pattern is refused and causes no side effect.

Round 1: reads outside the repository and a count search on /proc/PID/environ leaks the key. The plugin's own tools resolve every path against the repository root and refuse anything outside it; r3 tests outside paths, a symlink out of the repo, the run's HOME and /proc/self/environ.

Round 2: Hermes' search passed the pattern to rg without --, so --pre=rm ran commands. The plugin no longer calls Hermes' handler or any program; search uses Python re, r3 forbids subprocess, os.system, pty and shlex in the plugin and checks a --pre=rm pattern changes no file.

Nothing bounds how long the run takes, and the pure-Python search can hang it. A pattern such as (a+)+$ against a line of 40 a's and a b makes Python re backtrack for hours. CPython's re holds the GIL the whole time, so a timeout inside the plugin does not help: a ThreadPoolExecutor future.result(timeout=2) never returned (the probe was killed by an outer timeout at 30 s), Hermes' own future timeouts are stopped the same way, and signal.alarm only works on the main thread, while Hermes runs concurrent tool calls on worker threads (run_agent.py _execute_tool_calls_concurrent). A pattern-length limit does not help either, as the bad pattern is 7 characters. The workflow and action.yml set no timeout-minutes, so a hung audit holds a runner for GitHub's 6-hour default. Fix it outside the process: wrap hermes in `timeout` in knowledge-audit.sh and/or set timeout-minutes on the audit step. Matching literal text instead of a regex also works. Add a row condition that checks for the bound.

Round 1: reads outside the repository, and a count search on /proc/PID/environ, leaked the key. The plugin's own tools check every path against the root, now including each file the search opens and file symlinks; r3 tests outside paths, a symlink out, the run's HOME, /proc/self/environ and a file symlink.
Round 2: Hermes' search passed the pattern to rg with no --. The plugin starts no program; r3 forbids subprocess, os.system, pty and shlex and checks --pre=rm changes no file.

Round 3: a regex search could hang the process past any in-process timeout. Search now matches a plain substring (linear time), hermes runs under timeout MINUTES and the step has timeout-minutes; r2 checks the timeout with a sleeping stub and timeout-minutes in both files, r3 checks (a+)+$ returns within a second.

The plugin gives the auditor no way to find or list files by name. kmctl-auditor today has Read, Grep and Glob (plugin/agents/kmctl-auditor.md:4), and architecture-review step 3 requires checking that a page's list of files, hooks or stages matches the code's full list, where a missing item is drift (plugin/skills/architecture-review/SKILL.md:19-23); step 2 says 'find the file'. The plan's two tools are read one file and search file contents for text; the spike's search reused Hermes' search_files, whose schema has a file-name mode, but the new plain-Python search is described only as matching text in files, and no row checks name lookup or listing. Built as written, the auditor cannot see which files exist, so list checks become guesses: it either marks them unsure every time or calls a page holds without seeing the full list, which is the false result the audit exists to prevent. Fix: have kmctl_search_files also match file paths (substring, for example a target of content or names) or let kmctl_read_file list a folder, under the same root guard, and add an r3 condition that a name search or folder listing inside the root returns the files and one outside it is refused.

Round 1: reads outside the repository leaked the key through /proc. All three tools check every path against the root, file symlinks included; r3 tests outside paths, a symlink out, the run's HOME and /proc/self/environ for all three.
Round 2: Hermes' search passed the pattern to rg with no --. The plugin starts no program; r3 forbids subprocess, os.system, pty and shlex and checks --pre=rm changes no file.
Round 3: a regex could hang the process. Search and list match plain substrings; hermes runs under timeout and the step has timeout-minutes; r2 and r3 check both.

Round 4: the auditor could not find or list files by name. kmctl_list_files lists files under a folder, optionally filtered by a path substring, under the same root guard. That covers what Glob gave kmctl-auditor (plugin/agents/kmctl-auditor.md:4) for architecture-review's 'find the file' and list checks (plugin/skills/architecture-review/SKILL.md:16-23): list a folder, or filter by '.py' or a name. r3 now checks a file inside the root is listed and a folder outside returns nothing; r8 names the three tools.

kmctl_search_files numbers lines with str.splitlines(), which also breaks on \r, \x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, \x85 and U+2028, while kmctl_read_file numbers lines by \n. In a file holding a form feed or a lone \r, search reports a different line number than read for the same line, and the auditor cites path:line from search as evidence.

The whole prompt (skills, auditor text and the due list) goes to hermes as one argv string after -z. Linux caps one argument at 128 KiB (MAX_ARG_STRLEN), so a due list of roughly 800 or more concepts makes exec fail with E2BIG; the run then fails with "hermes exited 126" instead of a message that says why. The old script sent the prompt on stdin, so this ceiling is new.

The script unsets HERMES_PROFILE, HERMES_CONFIG, HERMES_ENV and HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS, but Hermes 0.19.0 also reads HERMES_MANAGED_DIR (hermes_cli/managed_scope.py), a managed config and .env applied last with override, which beats the config the script writes. It belongs in the same unset list.

entries.change: Search splits lines on newline only, dropping a trailing carriage return, as kmctl_read_file counts them, so path:line evidence agrees.
A file with a form feed and a lone carriage return gives the same line number from search and read.

findings.claim: kmctl_search_files numbered lines with str.splitlines(), so a form feed or lone CR gave search a different line number than read.
